newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy October car market to show signs of upturn.
newsitem.headline: Italy October car market to show signs of upturn.

text.p: Italy's depressed car market looks to be showing some signs of an upturn and new registrations data for October should be positive after heavy slumps in September and August, industry sources said.
Italy's Transport Ministry is due to publish new car registration figures for October on Saturday.
The sources said the October data should show two-digit year-on-year growth to above 130,000 units against 118,000 in October last year which was a poor month for Italian sales.
Italian September new car registrations fell 8.55 percent to 116,000 units, the worst September data for 12 years.
"The October data are very positive from a numerical point of view. There will be growth of quite a few percentage points," said one informed industry source who declined to be named.
"There's talk of a figure between 138,000 and 140,000 units, an increase of 15-17 percent. There could be downward correction but it would be a slight one," he added.

The recovery is likely to benefit foreign manufacturers as well as the Fiat Auto group. Fiat is expected to see its market share increase due the launch of the new "Marea" model range, the source added.
Fiat group new car registrations fell 17.48 percent in September year-on-year to 48,900 and its Italian market share dropped to 41.16 percent from 46.72 percent.
Another industry source said there would be growth in October "but I don't think new registrations will exceed 130,000 which would mean a rise of about 10 percent.
"I think growth of five to six percent would be more realistic," he added.
Another source said the October data would be good "but I don't think you can talk of a market recovery. However, the fact that there won't be another fall is positive."
Lorenzo Matthias, spokesman for Ford Italy, said "For us October has been a positive month with sales rising to 12,000 from 11,500 in October 1995."
In September, Ford saw new registrations of 10,000 against 9,935 in September last year.
Mercedes also saw a good October. "Our sales are in line with and perhaps slightly above September," a company spokesman said.
Mercedes registered September new registrations of 2,500 against 2,418 in the year-ago month.
